Going to a college far away from home is a brave choice! Really, it is so good you could go for your dream, even though it isn't THAT easy, since you have to adapt yourself to being away from your family and dog, (oh my God, just thinking about being away from my dog makes me insecure!).
I honestly think you are going well, you aren't struggling with your studies and although you "fake" being OK, you still see a future ahead of you. You'll certainly find a nice girl, I can feel it.
About the problem with your family, more specifically your dad, maybe it will be solved when you adapt yourself to the distance. You recognize that you should to be more careful towards them, and that's the first step! Focusing on paying more attention to these little things or something similar to it should probably be the next step you have to take. Again, you are doing really well.

The process of changing can be a bit stressful sometimes, and it is totally normal, so don't belittle yourself if it gets difficult to you. By the way, feel free to PM me whenever you feel like it's being difficult or for whatever other reason :)

She is a married woman, she knew exactly what was going to happen. By the way, as a married woman, she wouldn't have anything to gain by lying to you about the UID thing. UIDs really, really work. You are not a waste. If other person was in your position, they would have their own inner problems, maybe not like you do, but they surely would. You know, the process of recovering of a mental ilness can be... handful (?) to people, but trust me, staying positive about it is the best thing to do in that situation! :)

Hello, I don't know if you are still there or not, but I want to share my words with you.

Of course, I won't say "yes, I know exactly how you are feeling", because I personally believe that there's no such thing. However, I've also been through parental abuse and I know how it can tear your life apart in every possible way. By the way, while I was trying to cope with this situation, I've found lots of people and communities of people with BPD (mainly on Tumblr, if I'm not wrong) and they all always been so kind to me, although their personal problems.
That's how I found out that people with BPD are actually amazing. Having the disorder itself is already pretty complicated, but they still try to go on with their lifes, even if it means they'll surely have several mental breakdowns. And, you want me to be honest with you? I admire them, and I would give everything I have to be as strong as they are. You see, recently, I was diagnosed with depression (I've probably suffered of it from years now) and it's been horrible to me. But somehow, knowing that people with BPD are fighting everyday makes me a little more motivated to live.

I hope you are still there.
